w: The Chinati Foundation, also called La Fundacion Chinati, is a contemporary art museum in Marfa built entirely on the ideas of its founder, the minimalist artist Donald Judd. Rather than a general collection, it exists to realize one artist's own vision of how his work should be sited and seen.
s: A museum built on one artist's vision: Donald Judd
_facts: Contemporary art museum in Marfa, Texas
Also known as La Fundacion Chinati
Founded on the ideas of minimalist artist Donald Judd

w: Designed by El Paso's Trost & Trost in Spanish Revival style around a fountain courtyard, this 1930 hotel served area cattle ranchers for two decades. In summer 1955 it became the production base for Warner Bros' Giant, housing George Stevens and a cast that included James Dean, Elizabeth Taylor and Rock Hudson.
s: The 1930 hotel that housed the cast of Giant
_facts: Opened 1930, designed by Trost & Trost of El Paso in Spanish Revival style
Main clientele in the 1930s-40s were area cattle ranchers
Base for the Warner Bros. film Giant (1955), housing James Dean, Elizabeth Taylor, Rock Hudson
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places, 1978

w: Built of adobe in 1909 as the 'Mexican School,' this segregated schoolhouse taught Marfa's Hispanic children until 1965. After 1954 students were barred from speaking Spanish -- one alumna recalled a mock funeral held for the language. Alumni beat a 2006 demolition plan; it became a Park Service site in 2024.
s: A segregated 1909 schoolhouse, now a national historic site
_facts: Adobe schoolhouse built 1909, served Marfa's Hispanic students until 1965
Renamed for principal Jesse Blackwell in 1940; over 600 students at its peak
Post-1954 ban on speaking Spanish; students held a mock funeral for the language
Established as Blackwell School National Historic Site, July 2024
